title: Build Your GitHub Profile README
description: Create a professional GitHub profile README with intro, skills, stats, and project links
objective: Students will create a GitHub profile README repository, write a professional introduction in Markdown, add skill badges, GitHub stats widgets, and pin their best repositories

steps.title: Create Your Profile Repository
steps.instructions:
On GitHub:
1. Click **+** → **New repository**
2. Repository name: **your exact GitHub username** (e.g., if your username is `rahulsharma`, name the repo `rahulsharma`)
3. Check **Add a README file**
4. Click **Create repository**

This special repo's README appears on your GitHub profile page.

Clone it locally:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/YOUR_USERNAME.git
cd YOUR_USERNAME
```

Open `README.md` in VS Code.

steps.title: Write Your Introduction
steps.instructions:
Replace the README content with:

```markdown
# Hi, I'm Rahul Sharma 👋

**Full Stack Developer** | Python | FastAPI | HTML/CSS/JS

- 🎓 ADCA Graduate from TechPath Institute, Bhopal
- 💻 I build web applications and REST APIs
- 🌱 Currently learning: React, Docker, Cloud Deployment
- 📫 Reach me: rahul@email.com
- 🔗 Portfolio: [rahulsharma.github.io](https://rahulsharma.github.io)

---

## 🛠 Tech Stack

**Languages:** Python, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, SQL

**Frameworks:** FastAPI, Django, Bootstrap, Tailwind CSS

**Tools:** Git, VS Code, Docker, Postman, Figma

**Databases:** SQLite, MySQL

---

## 📂 Featured Projects

| Project | Description | Tech | Link |
|---------|-------------|------|------|
| Student API | REST API for student management | FastAPI, SQLite | [Repo](link) |
| Portfolio | Personal portfolio website | HTML, Tailwind | [Live](link) |
| Expense Tracker | Track daily expenses with charts | Python, Pandas | [Repo](link) |

---

## 📊 GitHub Stats

![GitHub Stats](https://github-readme-stats.vercel.app/api?username=YOUR_USERNAME&show_icons=true&theme=default)

![Top Languages](https://github-readme-stats.vercel.app/api/top-langs/?username=YOUR_USERNAME&layout=compact)
```

Replace `YOUR_USERNAME` with your actual GitHub username.

Commit and push:
```bash
git add README.md
git commit -m "Add profile README with intro, badges, and stats"
git push
```

Visit your GitHub profile — the README should appear at the top.

steps.title: Pin Your Best Repositories
steps.instructions:
On your GitHub profile page:
1. Click **Customize your pins**
2. Select 4-6 of your best repositories
3. Make sure each pinned repo has:
   - A clear description (edit in repo Settings)
   - Topics/tags (add via repo homepage → gear icon near About)
   - A README with: what it does, how to run it, screenshots

For each pinned repo, verify:
- [ ] Description is filled in
- [ ] README exists with setup instructions
- [ ] No sensitive files (`.env`, passwords)
- [ ] Code is clean and organized

Visit your profile in a private/incognito window to see how it looks to others.

steps.title: Review and Get Feedback
steps.instructions:
Do a final review of your GitHub profile:

1. Open your profile in **incognito/private window** (so you see what others see)

2. Check this list:
- [ ] Profile photo is set (professional or avatar)
- [ ] Bio is filled in (one-line description)
- [ ] README loads and looks good
- [ ] Badges render correctly (no broken images)
- [ ] GitHub Stats widget shows your data
- [ ] At least 4 repos are pinned
- [ ] Each pinned repo has a description and README
- [ ] No embarrassing repo names ("test", "untitled", "asdfgh")
- [ ] No sensitive files visible in any repo (.env, passwords)

3. Ask a batchmate to review your profile and give feedback:
- What's the first impression?
- Is it clear what you do?
- Can they find your best work easily?
- Any broken links or missing info?

4. Make fixes based on feedback and push updates.

**Submit:** Your GitHub profile URL + screenshot in incognito + batchmate's feedback (2-3 sentences).

expected_output: A professional GitHub profile page with a README containing introduction, tech stack badges, featured projects table, GitHub stats widgets, and 4+ pinned repositories with proper descriptions
